page: Amazon Web Services m9g.8xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the Nitro System and custom AWS Graviton processors based on the 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 architecture. The instance provides 32 dedicated physical cores running at 3.3 GHz with a single thread per core, avoiding resource contention from simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation totals 128.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The processor features 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of dedicated L2 cache per core, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. Baseline network throughput is configured at 17 Gbps.

The compute profile demonstrates top-tier efficiency across general-purpose execution metrics. In Geekbench testing, the instance registers scores in the top 10 percent for single-core execution at 2390.0 and multi-core processing at 25914.0, alongside strong compiler throughput during Clang builds at 62746.0. Memory subsystem testing reflects strong performance with PassMark memory scoring in the top 10 percent and cached 16 KB read bandwidth reaching 4569.26 GB/sec. Data manipulation is equally fast, with single-threaded compression benchmarks such as gzip and bzip3 placing in the top decile. In-memory data store performance is supported by Redis SET throughput reaching 92.33 million operations per second.

Hardware tradeoffs include the complete absence of local NVMe storage, meaning all persistent data relies on remote network storage volumes over the 17 Gbps network link. Furthermore, with zero GPU acceleration, the server is unsuitable for heavy machine learning model training or heavy text generation, as reflected in bottom-quartile small-model LLM generation benchmarks. The instance delivers high resource density and operational cost efficiency for scale-out architectures, software compilation pipelines, relational and caching databases, and high-concurrency static web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services m9g.8xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 32 dedicated physical cores built on the 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 architecture at 3.3 GHz. Paired with 128.0 GB of system memory, it adheres to a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio supported by 48 MB of L3 cache and a 17 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results reveal top-tier compute performance in multi-core compilation, data compression, and PassMark database operations, complemented by strong cached memory bandwidth. The instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, meaning workloads rely on network volumes and CPU execution alone. Text generation on large language models shows performance constraints, reflecting the absence of hardware accelerators. Consequently, m9g.8xlarge offers strong resource efficiency for high-concurrency web serving, CI/CD compilation pipelines, caching layers, and database workloads requiring dedicated non-hyperthreaded physical cores.
